clues.text: In the garden of Eden, it was more crafty than any beast of the field the LORD God had made.
After the fall in Eden, God cursed it to go on its belly and eat dust all its days.
God said the woman's seed would crush its head in Eden, and it would strike his heel.
When Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, the staff became this.
When Israelites were bitten in the wilderness, God told Moses to make a fiery one and mount it on a pole.
In John's vision, an angel seized this ancient one, called the devil and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.
In John's vision, it spewed water like a river from its mouth to sweep the woman away.
